text:
alice_customer: Hi, our API p99 jumped up to ~12s and ~5% 500s across the last 2 hours. We also saw GPU OOMs on model-server gpu-7. Tenant: acme-corp-42. example req: r_83ab

sara_support: Sorry about that — escalating to runtime. @vikram_eng @jessica_runtime can you take a look? We're on hosted us-west2.

alice_customer: We're on hosted, model gpt4-mini-8k-quant, lots of short chat turns + occasional very long context (~8k tokens). Sudden bursty traffic since 03:10 PST.

ops-bot: alert: gpu-oom detected node=gpu-7 at 5051234501 (oom_killer engaged)

vikram_eng: looking. Initial telemetry shows KV cache size for acme-corp-42 increased ~3x vs baseline in last hour. Allocator logs show many small allocation failures then slow fallback path — likely fragmentation + KV growth.

jessica_runtime: can you paste the allocator/log snippet and a sample request trace id? any retries?

alice_customer: trace r_83ab attached: `{"seq":24,"tokens":7800,...}`. No retries from client, just front-end concurrency spikes.

vikram_eng: hypothesis: KV growth from long contexts + bursty concurrency -> slab fragmentation -> OOM -> runtime falling back to slower allocator path causing p99 spikes.

vikram_eng: quick mitigations we can do now:
1) throttle tenant concurrency (reduce simultaneous sessions)
2) bump eviction aggressiveness for tenant KV cache
3) rolling restart of affected pods to defragment GPU slab and reclaim fragmented memory
4) recommend customer reduce max_context to 4k until we stabilize

jessica_runtime: commands to run (internal admin CLI):
```
redwood admin tenant update --id acme-corp-42 --max-concurrency 8
redwood runtime evict-policy set --tenant acme-corp-42 --policy aggressive
```

jessica_runtime: if we need a manual compaction: run internal compactor on nodes with fragmentation >65%:
```
infra-bot run compactor --node gpu-7 --force
```

luisa_sre: alternative: move tenant temporarily to big-gpu pool (A100-80GB) to relieve pressure while we root cause. That buys headroom without restart.

sara_support: I'm applying the concurrency limit + evict policy now. Will notify when done.

ops-bot: command executed by sara_support at 5051234520: `admin tenant update acme-corp-42 --concurrency=8`

ops-bot: command executed by sara_support at 5051234522: `runtime evict-policy set acme-corp-42 aggressive`

jessica_runtime: scheduling rolling restarts on the 3 pods in the `us-west2-runtime` pool that touched acme-corp-42. will do 1 at a time to avoid impact. start 5051234550.

alice_customer: after the changes (applied ~5 mins ago) latency p99 dropped to ~2.1s and 500s down to 0.5%. thanks! :grinning:

vikram_eng: great — follow-ups I'm creating:
- RN-1123: add per-tenant KV size cap with early-stall/429 to avoid runaway growth
- RN-1124: slab fragmentation alert (fraction > 0.65) -> auto-compactor trigger + page-scan diagnostics
- RN-1125: allocator tuning: experiment with slab_target_fill=0.75 for smaller per-alloc fragmentation

These will be assigned to eng-runtime.

jessica_runtime: added a short diagnostic routine for support to run if this recurs:
```
curl -s https://int-api.redwood/diag?tid=acme-corp-42
# returns slab usage, kv-size-by-tenant, top-10 traces by tokens
```

luisa_sre: temporary mitigation note: if you see node-level OOMs >2 within 30m, escalate to infra to move tenant to big-gpu pool automatically.

sara_support: I'll keep the customer updated and monitor for 24h. leaving this thread open until stable.

alice_customer: Thanks all for the fast turnaround! We'll keep an eye and report if it reappears. :rocket:

jessica_runtime: if it reappears pls include one trace id and the `diag` output; it speeds root cause.

vikram_eng: logging: RN-1123/4/5 created and linked to this thread. tagging for visibility: @eng-runtime @eng-infra.

sara_support: resolved for now, will reopen on recurrence. Closing loop to customer in CRM.

infra-bot: note: next steps scheduled: compactor-run on gpu-7 at 5051234800 if fragmentation stays >0.6

sara_support: marking last_message_ts=5051234620 in thread metadata.
